meaning: Act-1 coffee-break driver entry: dispatches on the cutscene sub-state byte #4e06 via the 7-word table at #210c (sub-states 0..6). The whole act-1 scene is this position-threshold machine, not a frame-counted animation.
Sub-state 0 ends when Pac's tile byte #4d3a == #21 (Pac walks in from the start tile while Blinky is frozen). `sub #21` on the tile byte.

Sub-state 1 (the chase, both actors moving) ends when Pac's tile byte #4d3a == #1e. `sub #1e`. NOTE: this bare comparison shows no wrap/reset; THIS PORT closes the 0x21->0x1e gap via the 8-bit counter wrap (keeping one forward step-sign), an inference of the port's, not a mechanism this cite demonstrates.
Sub-state 2 (Blinky alone) ends when Blinky's tile byte #4d32 == #1e; on that edge the ROM frightens all ghosts (#1a70) and reverses the actors (#05ae, `4d3c = 4d30 ^ 2`). `sub #1e`.
Sub-state 4 (the frightened Blinky fleeing, reversed vector) ends when Blinky's tile byte #4d32 == #2f. `sub #2f`.
Sub-state 5 (big-Pac chasing, both moving) ends when Blinky's tile byte #4d32 == #3d. `sub #3d`.
Sub-state 6 (big-Pac closing) ends — and the whole scene ends — when Pac's tile byte #4d3a == #3d. `sub #3d`.
Act-1 actor-layout routine #260f seeds Pac's tile pair #4d39/#4d3a with the word #1f32 -> the high (tile) byte #4d3a = #1f, Pac's cutscene start column.
Act-1 actor-layout routine #260f seeds the ghost tile pairs (#4d31/#4d33/#4d35/#4d37) with the word #1e32 -> the high (tile) byte = #1e, Blinky's cutscene start column, one tile behind Pac.

big-Pac sprite routine #15e6 reads the cutscene sub-state #4e06 (#15e6 `ld a,(#4e06)`) and gates on `sub #05; ret c` (#15e9/#15eb): the value 5 is the #15e9 immediate byte itself, so the big-Pac (four 16x16 sprites, colour #16) is drawn ONLY when the sub-state >= 5 — i.e. from the return leg onward. Cited to the compare instruction #15e9, not the load #15e6, so a drift in the #05 operand reddens (the H1-R2/168f discipline).

Pac's normal mouth animation reads the sprite pixel low byte #4d09 (#168c) and masks `and #07` (#168f): 4 mouth images across an 8-pixel cycle (a new image every 2px, thresholds 2/4/6 at #1691..#16a7). The 8-length is the mask #07 + 1 — cited to the mask instruction itself (#168f), the same anchor as the sibling big-Pac #15ef `and #0f` claim.

big-Pac's mouth reads the same sprite pixel low byte #4d09 (#15ec) and masks `and #0f` (#15ef): the SAME 4 images across a 16-value cycle (thresholds 4/8/c at #15f1..#1601) — half the cadence rate of Pac's `and #07` 8-cycle. The 16-length is the mask #0f + 1.

The ghost leg-wiggle counter #4dc4 is incremented each frame (#0e26), compared to 8 (#0e27 `ld a,#08`, #0e29 `cp (hl)`) and reset to 0 on match (#0e2b `ld (hl),#00`) — an 8-frame toggle period. The value 8 is the #0e27 immediate byte.

The return-leg Blinky is the BLUE FRIGHTENED sprite: the frighten-all routine #1a70 sets the ghost sprite image to #1c (`ld (ix+#02),#1c`) with colour #11. This is act 1's chased-back ghost — NOT the ripped sheet (#32/#33, #162d, act 2).
